title: Treat MCP transport EOF as closed
summary: MCP subprocess servers can exit or EOF unexpectedly. The stdio MCP client currently surfaces EOF as a synthetic JSON-RPC error; normalize it to a first-class transport closed error so callers can handle crashes and shutdowns predictably.
expectedFailureModes: Tool bootstrap hangs or returns opaque errors when the MCP server exits after initialize.
EOF on stdout is reported as a JSON-RPC error instead of McpClientError::Closed, making error handling inconsistent.
Docs/tests claim in-flight requests resolve with Closed but actual behavior diverges.
nextAction: Map the internal EOF drain error to McpClientError::Closed, extend the fake MCP server to exit after initialize, and add a live stdio test that asserts bootstrap fails with a transport-closed error.
